title: Sharp Degree Boundary for Gaussian Approximation of Additive SNIPE under Bernoulli Assignment
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < 7.4. Math and decision pass; not salvageable within scope. Independent main validity-gate confirms terminal below floor.
gap_reasons: The supplied proofs establish the whole-class cubic degree boundary, including arbitrary mixed variance shares, legal unchanged-floor counterexamples, and explicit boundary laws for the fixed fair-Bernoulli additive estimator. This classification extends the bounded-degree sufficiency of [CEY (2023), Theorem 3](https://maeichho.github.io/publication/jci23/jci23.pdf); the indicator-Stein leaf is covered by the cited [Nourdin–Peccati (2009), Section 2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0803.0458v3). Sharpness concerns the vanishing regime: the upper modulus 220(d³/n)^(1/5) and lower modulus d/√n do not establish the optimal quantitative error, which remains explicitly open. Practical significance is constrained by an upper bound that is trivial unless n/d³ exceeds 220⁵, a worst-case variance envelope without efficiency guarantees, and examples that demonstrate failure mechanisms without establishing interval informativeness at realistic scales. The 'Honest scope' assertions that all statements and the downstream probability proof remain owed contradict the displayed proofs and require editorial correction, but the TL;DR does not falsely claim completion of the open modulus problem. The projected score reflects a specialized fixed-estimator classification with limited finite-sample calibration value, rather than a broadly applicable inference framework. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

Independent boundary and main validity consults: no bounded same-topic repair reaches field; quantitative modulus, realistic finite-sample calibration, schedule-sensitive variance control and broader scope require new core research.
proof_attempt_summary: A field-targeted additive SNIPE whole-class Gaussian frontier was derived and received math and decision PASS; the indicator-Stein leaf was independently source-attested and verified. Final D0.5 assessed the delivered result as subfield with score ceiling 6.7 below 7.4, independently confirmed terminal by both boundary and main validity consults: novelty framing, not the mathematical kernel, fell short. The optimal Kolmogorov modulus and useful schedule-sensitive finite-sample inference remain open; F stages and Lean/type-checker verification were not reached, and stale honest_scope prose is disclosed rather than treated as a mathematical failure.
tldr: Canonical additive SNIPE has a sharp whole-class Gaussian degree boundary under independent fair Bernoulli assignment. In the newly defined regime with both directed degrees at most \(d\), raw row coefficient mass at most one, and design variance at least \((100n)^{-1}\), the worst-case standardized Kolmogorov error vanishes exactly when \(d^3/n\to0\). Self-loops are permitted rather than required, and the same boundary holds on the explicitly self-inclusive retained restriction. The theorem includes an explicit unoptimized upper bound, legal nonnegative monotone failure schedules on every excluded subsequence at the unchanged numerical floor, and finite-switch non-Gaussian boundary laws. An attainable graph-only variance envelope supports uniformly conservative connected normal intervals inside that regime. The optimal quantitative order of the Gaussian error remains open.
gap: SNIPE has an unbiased total-effect functional and sufficient normality results, but the inherited source survey does not classify uniform Gaussianity over an explicit fixed numerical variance-floor regime when both directed degrees grow. The published graph model permits self-loops, and its CLT requires scaled variance to converge to a positive constant; neither universal self-inclusion nor the numerical floor is its standard assumption. The accepted prior proposal supplies estimation risk and explicitly excludes inference. Generic Rademacher approximation does not provide a legal causal converse by itself.
fill: Uniform mixed-error sufficiency and an integer-packed causal converse give the matched degree boundary. The exact graph envelope also characterizes which graph slices admit the retained floor and supplies conservative intervals. These claims support future known-network additive fair-Bernoulli rollout analyses with externally justified coefficient bounds.
